h1: Parida Resort — A Quiet Little Garden Resort in Phrom Buri, Sing Buri
intro: If you're after Sing Buri accommodation that feels like a quiet little garden resort with spacious rooms, balconies and an easy price tag rather than a busy town hotel — Parida Resort is a small property in Phrom Buri district, Ban Mo subdistrict · It has around 9 rooms set in a leafy garden, with a small kids' water-play area, sit-out balconies, free private parking and free Wi-Fi · Guests consistently praise the spacious, clean rooms, the quiet, and the value, while the trade-off is the location about 20 km from Sing Buri town — you'll need your own car, and there are no shops within walking distance · Rooms start from approx. ฿590/night

body.html: Parida Resort is a small property in Ban Mo subdistrict, Phrom Buri district, in the southern part of Sing Buri province · It's a handful-of-rooms place (around 9 rooms) set in a leafy garden, with a small kids' water-play area, sit-out balconies and free private parking — well suited to self-drive travellers who want a quiet, affordable base or a road-trip stopover around Phrom Buri · Because it's so small, the feel is homey and informal rather than a full-service hotel with every amenity on tap.

Rooms come in a few types, from the Deluxe King (a big bed, about 21 sqm) and Standard Twin (two single beds, about 22 sqm) up to a Queen Family Room of around 50 sqm that's great for families · Inside you get air-conditioning, a flat-screen TV, an electric kettle, an en-suite bathroom, and many rooms have a private balcony or terrace looking onto the garden · What guests mention most is that rooms are spacious, clean and quiet, and good value — especially the family room, which gives you a lot of space for the money · The trade-off to understand is that a small resort like this doesn't have staff on site around the clock the way a big hotel does; at some times you may need to call ahead or arrange your arrival.
"The room was big, clean and very quiet, with a garden for the kids to run around and a little water-play area they loved · Parking was easy and the price was low — perfect for a stopover."

What sets Parida apart from a town hotel is the quiet garden setting and the small kids' water-play area · Plenty of reviews talk about coming as a family, the kids having space to play while the adults relax in the garden with no noise · But as a small resort the amenities are basic — there's no in-house restaurant, and the water play is a small feature rather than a big water park · One thing to be aware of is that the review base is still thin (around 9 reviews) because the property is small and off the radar, so the overall score of around 7.2 is solid for a budget stay but isn't drawn from a large pool of reviews.

Location is the thing to be clear about before booking · Parida Resort sits in Ban Mo, Phrom Buri, about 20 km from Sing Buri town — a quiet rural area surrounded by temples and fields, with no convenience store or restaurant within walking distance · It's close to several Phrom Buri temples such as Wat Sa Ket and Wat Sing, and not far from the Chao Phraya River, which makes it a handy base for temple visits or a break along the route if you're driving · If you want to eat or buy supplies you'll have to drive out, so plan your meals ahead.

Honestly, Parida Resort does its job well on its own terms — a quiet stay, spacious rooms, a garden and a kids' water feature — but it is not a luxury resort or a full-service town hotel · If you want a central place you can walk around, or full service with breakfast, Chaisaeng Villa Hotel or Chaisaeng Palace Hotel in town would suit you better · But if you want a quiet garden stay at an easy price, you're coming as a family with young kids, and you don't mind driving out for everything — this delivers value and calm that are hard to find at the same price.

A tip from following the reviews here: always contact the resort to confirm before you travel, since a small place may need you to arrange a check-in time or have the water-play area switched on in advance · If you're a group or a family, ask for the larger Queen Family Room — it's great value · Plan for food, because there's nothing within walking distance: bring supplies in the car or plan to drive into town · And compare Agoda and Booking prices before you book every time, as rates shift by season and small places sometimes have platform-specific deals.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Parida Resort Sing Buri

faq.q: Where is Parida Resort in Sing Buri, and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's at 142 Moo 4, Ban Mo, Phrom Buri, in the southern part of Sing Buri province · It's a quiet rural area about 20 km from Sing Buri town · It's near several Phrom Buri temples such as Wat Sa Ket and Wat Sing, and not far from the Chao Phraya River and Ang Thong's Wat Chaiyo Worawihan · There are no restaurants or convenience stores within walking distance, so you'll need to drive out.

faq.q: How much does Parida Resort cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rooms start from approx. ฿590/night for the Deluxe King · There's also a Standard Twin (two single beds) and a Queen Family Room of around 50 sqm that's great for families · Prices rise on weekends and holidays, so compare a few platforms before you book.

faq.q: Who is Parida Resort best for?
faq.a: It's great for families or self-drive travellers wanting a quiet little garden resort with spacious rooms at an easy price · Kids get a water-play feature and a garden to run around in, and it works well as a base for Phrom Buri temples or a road-trip stopover · It's not for people who want a central place they can walk around, or a full-service resort.

faq.q: Does Parida Resort have a pool or water play?
faq.a: There's a small kids' water-play area in the garden, which families in the reviews enjoy · But it's a small feature, not a big water park or full swimming pool · It's worth contacting the resort to confirm it'll be open when you visit, as a small place may need to arrange it ahead.

faq.q: Does Parida Resort have breakfast or a restaurant?
faq.a: Parida Resort is a small property with no in-house restaurant, and there's nothing within walking distance · It's best to bring supplies in the car or plan to drive into Sing Buri town to eat · Rooms have an electric kettle for drinks, and there's a 24-hour front desk with luggage storage.

faq.q: What's Parida Resort's review score, and is it reliable?
faq.a: Parida Resort is a small resort of around 9 rooms with a score of about 7.2 from real guest reviews, which is solid for a budget stay · Note that the review base is still thin (around 9 reviews) because the property is small and off the radar, so the figure isn't from a large pool · Its strengths are spacious rooms, quiet and value — best for travellers who understand they're booking a small rural resort, not a town hotel.
